A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ZeroSiam research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet-C adaptation experiments, mathematical reasoning evaluations, efficiency measurements and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds sensitivity, adaptation-duration, repeated-seed and multi-branch comparison results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the architecture and the adaptation objective remain unchanged. Appendix E.6 adds a supplementary procedure for selecting the predictor learning rate by minimizing prediction-entropy change after adaptation on Gaussian noise; it does not replace the fixed rates in the main experiments.

E1.justification: The datasets and vision/language tasks are retained. Table 11 adds actual evaluation at ImageNet-C severity levels 1 and 3, extending the severity-5 alpha study in v1 Table F to milder corruption conditions.

E2.justification: New Table J evaluates SPA and TTE on ResNet50-GN and ViT-Base, and REM on ViT-Base. These directly relevant multi-branch comparisons substantially broaden the evaluated comparator set; the original comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds distinct supplementary protocols: three- and five-epoch adaptation, calibration using 6,400 Gaussian inputs, and accuracy/memory/time comparisons with efficiency measured on an A100 at batch size 64. The original RTX 3090 timing experiment and main adaptation settings remain, so these are added evaluations rather than replacements.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis with entropy-versus-divergence trajectories, Swin-Tiny learning-rate sensitivity, noise-based calibration validation, adaptation-duration robustness and a norm-inflation diagnostic. The alpha study gains additional severities. Existing collapse-recovery and stop-gradient analyses are retained, with the latter moving to E.8/Table H.

E5.justification: v1 does not disclose repeated-run counts or uncertainty estimates. Appendix E.9 explicitly reports five-seed reruns of the label-shift comparison for DeYO and ZeroSiam across five architectures, with means and standard deviations in Table I, adding substantial statistical support for stability.

E6.justification: DeYO's Table 3 overall average changes from 44.4% to 43.1%, and its Swin-Tiny average in Table A changes from 43.1% to 36.5%. New results cover calibration, uncertainty, efficiency and longer adaptation, including ZeroSiam's 65.7% at epochs three and five in Table G. The earlier alpha=3 result of 61.0% is omitted.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, both lemmas, the formal assumptions and Appendix B proofs are retained. Appendix E.10 adds mathematical definitions of decision margin and relative boundary sharpness, together with scaling reasoning about logit-norm inflation.

C1.justification: The introduction newly claims to be the first study of asymmetric structure in TTA, strengthening the explicit novelty claim. The central contributions concerning efficient collapse prevention, biased-signal regularization and vision/language adaptation retain their earlier scope.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands explanations of shortcuts, alpha's balancing role and gradient interference from norm inflation. Appendix E.6 adds a concrete limitation: entropy-based Gaussian calibration may fail for ConvNeXt. E.11 further develops applicability arguments, while the original limited success of collapse recovery remains acknowledged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a ZeroSiam source-code link, explicitly identifies the main evaluations as one epoch, and supplies calibration sample counts, learning-rate settings and A100 measurement details. Appendix C's existing optimizer, model and LoRA specifications are largely unchanged; the new reproducibility statement mainly organizes existing information.

R1.justification: New Appendix E.11 substantially positions ZeroSiam against SPA, REM and TTE through differences in architecture, augmentation, collapse assumptions and efficiency. REM, TTE, OT-VP and DPCore references are added, several other TTA references are removed, and the introduction strengthens the first-in-TTA novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Efficient Siamese' to 'Efficient Asymmetry', with selected abstract, introduction and mechanism paragraphs rewritten. The alpha discussion moves into the main text, and acknowledgments, ethics, reproducibility and LLM-use statements are added. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds two plots and new calibration, epoch, statistical and multi-branch comparison tables. Old Table F becomes the expanded main-text Table 11; old Table G becomes Table H, and Table 2 is relocated. These substantially expand the visual presentation while retaining the original architecture and principal result displays.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in v1's central stability and efficiency argument through five-seed uncertainty estimates and direct multi-branch comparisons in Tables I and J. Additional duration and sensitivity tests strengthen practical reliability evidence, and the source-code link improves reproducibility information. Figure F's evaluation scope remains ambiguous, but this localized weakness does not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical substantiation.
